reason: The bone-lineage environment signals a subset of stem-cell descendants to develop toward bone-forming cells, matching the chapter's first task.
expectation: The population will begin developing along the bone-cell lineage.

effect: The lineage produced osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, ready to contribute to the mature bone model.
reaction: The distinction between matrix-producing and embedded bone cells is useful.
reason: The chapter calls for assembling the bone's collagen and mineral; the crystals plausibly reinforce the fibrous framework.
expectation: The mineral will combine with the collagen framework to form a strengthened bone structure.

effect: The framework now contains mineral, illustrating how collagen and mineral contribute different mechanical properties.
reaction: The contrast between toughness and compression resistance is helpful.
reason: The chapter says to assemble mature bone with its living cells, so the bone cells belong with the mineralised framework.
expectation: The framework will gain living bone cells, including embedded osteocytes.

effect: The mineralised bones now contain connected living cells; blood vessels are still available to supply the bone.
reaction: The tiny channels make the cells' connections inside hard bone clearer.
reason: Blood vessels should support the living cells in the bone before the elbow is assembled.
expectation: The arm bones will gain a blood supply.

effect: The bones now have vessels supplying nutrients to their embedded cells, leaving the elbow joint to assemble.
reaction: The distinction between blood cells staying in vessels and nutrients leaving them is clear.
reason: Articular cartilage should cap the bone ends where they meet at the elbow.
expectation: The bone ends will gain smooth cartilage surfaces for the joint.

effect: The elbow-facing bone surfaces now have smooth cartilage caps, leaving the capsule and ligaments to assemble.
reaction: The sliding-surface inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The synovial capsule should enclose the cartilage-covered joint and its fluid.
expectation: The elbow joint will gain a fluid-containing capsule.

effect: The capsule now encloses the joint, and its lining supplies fluid to help the surfaces glide.
reaction: The connection between the lining and joint fluid is clear.
reason: The remaining elbow ligaments should span and support the enclosed joint.
expectation: The ligaments will stabilize the elbow while allowing it to move.

effect: The ligaments completed the movable arm skeleton, showing bending alongside resistance to sideways movement; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The final cutaway ties the joint components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mineralising the collagen framework was most worthwhile: the planned comparison connects collagen's toughness and mineral's compression resistance to the bone's structure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cartilage and then the capsule felt somewhat predictable, although their planned cutaways clearly distinguish sliding surfaces from the fluid-containing enclosure.

surprise.text: The lineage picture shows some matrix-producing osteoblasts becoming embedded osteocytes, linking bone formation to the living cells inside mature bone.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the sequence of adding cells and vessels to a separate mature-bone framework is a modelling convention rather than a literal account of how bone develops.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions connect cell-scale processes to mechanical function, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than this chapter's largely straightforward sequence.
